seat.BEST_WHY: The floor in the lit zone around the figure (roughly x 200–650, y 460–720) is cut stone, not a stamp: courses are staggered, block widths vary from ~25px to ~90px along a single row, and joints change depth — the row directly below the figure has a deep dark joint on its left half and a shallow one on its right. The south-facing wall face (band at y≈425–450) is modelled as a separate surface: darker bricks with vertical driven pins breaking the course, and it takes the figure's light at a different intensity from the wall top above it, so wall top / wall face / floor read as three planes. The lighting falloff is handled in value AND hue — warm cream at the figure, desaturating to blue-grey at the bottom-right corner (x 600–740, y 800–900) — rather than a plain black multiply.
seat.WORST_WHY: The pool (x 248–335, y 0–190) is a flat teal rectangle with a razor-straight edge butting directly against the dirt floor — no bank, no edge tile, no shoreline transition; a filled rect. The fill itself is a faint hexagonal honeycomb pattern (visible at 8×), which is a procedural noise, not painted water. The lilypads sit on it with no shadow or ripple. The two chests at (60–95, 0–20) and (60–95, 45–65) are pixel-identical duplicates, and they are drawn in side elevation (gold lid above, dark plank front below) inside a top-down world where the barrels at (115–195, 190–220) are drawn from directly above. The grey slabs are a flat fill with a 1px grid line and a handful of speckles; the moss is the same translucent teal blob stamped at (20–60, 50–75), (15–50, 200–230) and (350–380, 150–170). The dirt is rust-speckle noise with no structure. Every surface is uniformly lit; nothing in the frame is modelled in value.

_what: THE ITEM'S OWN MEASURED EXIT — required by INSTALL-LATEST (Rafe, 2026-09-08).
A build installs because it DID THE THING IT SET OUT TO DO. The rank test only says
the doing cost nothing against the seeded reference; this says what was done. Without
it, 'not worse than the reference' would mean 'not different from it', and a round
that changed nothing would install as readily as one that fixed something.
Declared here per item, recorded into the verdict, re-checked at the gate. The gate
refuses a `met` with no measurement behind it.

law: LOOP-PROCESS: an art round is judged by eyes on delivered frames. The plant must land worst-or-flagged; a passed plant voids the round and its findings are not read. The guards measure progress — rank in the deck — never rounds elapsed.
